newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Palm Oil/Laurics- Southeast Asia prices seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Palm Oil/Laurics- Southeast Asia prices seen mixed.

text.p: Southeast Asian palm and laurics oil prices may be mixed this week with the palm market looking for direction from official Malaysian August crop data expected at 0430 GMT, regional traders said.
They said the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) announcement of August output/export/stock palm oil figures could provide an early lead on the possible trend of prices.
Crop forecaster Ivan Wong on Friday estimated August output would rise by 11 percent to 801,000 tonnes, with end-August stock at 785,000 tonnes and exports at 680,000 tonnes.
"We expect some supportive data from PORLA today," a dealer in Kuala Lumpur said.
But some Singapore traders said prices could fall.

"India is at the tail end of its buying and is now waiting for its harvest, Pakistan is out and the Chinese find the current prices too high. Demand is not going to pick up from here," one Singapore trader said.
He said the devaluation of the rupee in Pakistan, a possible decline in Indian purchases due to domestic vegetable oil harvests and the absence of China would affect the market.
Other Singapore dealers were more cautious and predicted the market would move sideways.
"There's a lot of mixed signals in the market. The next indication for prices will be the data, and it should move sideways for now," a dealer at a Western commodity house in Singapore said.
Malaysia's third month November futures could slide further if there is no aggressive demand, dealers said.

In Indonesia, traders said prices could soften further on the prospect of additional palm oil supply from state commodity regulator BULOG in the short-term. BULOG said on Wednesday it planned to buy an additional 30,000 tonnes of CPO from state plantations to stabilise market prices.
"Buyers will be waiting for prices to soften due to the additional supply," one trader in Medan said.
Some Indonesian traders were also waiting for PORLA data to determine market trends.
On Friday, Indonesian palm olein was quoted at 1,425-30 rupiah/kg in Medan and 1,455-60 rupiah/kg in Jakarta.
Philippines coconut oil prices were expected to firm this week on demand and tight supply in major production areas, dealers said.
"Prices strengthened in the past two days with demand picking up in both local and overseas markets as manufacturing companies stocked up on inventories," a Manila trader said on Friday.
Philippine traders said the buying price of coconut oil for nearby months rose to $745 CIF per tonne late on Friday against $720 at the start of the last week.
"Prices could still rise this week due to tight copra supply in key producing areas in the Philippines," another trader said.
Traders said they expect Philippine coconut oil shipments overseas to increase to between 60,000 and 70,000 tonnes this month against 56,000 tonnes in August.
(with contributions from Singapore/Jakarta/Manila)
-- KUALA LUUMPUR newsroom 603-230-8911)
